subject: Recap: Redwood + FintechX discovery — unit economics & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fintechx.com>, Priya Agarwal <priya.agarwal@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T16:05:00Z
Subject: Recap: Redwood + FintechX discovery — unit economics & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time and the clear context on your roadmap. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment before sending a detailed quote: 

Summary of needs
- Use cases: real-time customer support summarization (high QPS, low latency), document ingestion for onboarding (batch embeddings), and in-chat credit-decision assistance (medium latency, higher context windows).
- Target regions: US primary, EU later.

Requested follow-ups
1) Volume & unit economics: can you confirm MAUs, average sessions per MAU, and average tokens per session (we discussed ballpark numbers on the call). We need monthly token volume to map to $/1M token tiers.
2) Budget range: high/low monthly budget range helps us propose the right model tier (hosted vs dedicated).
3) Feature prioritization: please attach any internal prioritization if available so we can map $/feature impact.

Quick note on economics we discussed
- Typical hosted pricing bands we expect to propose: $10–$35 per 1M tokens depending on model family and quantization.
- For large steady volumes (>500M tokens/mo) Dedicated or Reserved pricing becomes more economical; we can model both.

Next steps
- If you can share the usage workbook you mentioned, we’ll run a unit-econ model and send a 1-2 page deep-dive mapping $/feature and CAC payback scenarios by Thursday.
- I’ll loop in Aditya (cc) to scope any eval runs needed (sample payloads, latency SLOs).

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (pricing bands + model variants)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — attaching the usage workbook you asked for (FintechX_usage_workbook.xlsx). High-level answers below so you can start modeling: 

- MAUs (monthly active users): 250,000
- Avg sessions per MAU per month: 3
- Avg tokens per session: ~1,200 (average across chat/summary flows; decision-assist flows spike higher ~3k)
- Expected launch ramp: pilot month ~10% of MAU, full launch in 3 months to 60-70% of MAU.
- Target monthly budget (ballpark): $30k- $80k; execs prefer to see both a conservative and aggressive P&L.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you model $/feature (e.g., summary, decision-assist, embeddings) so we can map revenue per MAU to cost?
- Include an example CAC payback scenario assuming 20% NRR uplift and $50 CAC per new MAU.

Thanks — attaching: FintechX_usage_workbook.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood + FintechX discovery — unit economics deep-dive (draft)

Samir —

Appreciate the workbook — we ran the initial model against three scenarios (pilot, steady-state conservative, steady-state aggressive). Below is a concise unit-econ summary and the key levers that change gross margin & payback. I’ll attach the one-page PDF with the worked calcs after you confirm this aligns.

Assumptions (from your workbook + conservative defaults)
- MAU steady-state: 250k
- Sessions/Mo per MAU: 3
- Avg tokens/session: 1,200 (chat/summary mix), decision-assist avg 3,000 but only 10% of requests
- Monthly tokens (conservative): 250k * 3 * 1,200 = 900M tokens/mo

Redwood pricing scenarios (hosted) — illustrative list price ranges
- General-purpose model (quantized): $25 per 1M tokens
- High-efficiency model: $15 per 1M tokens
- Dedicated/reserved: effective $8- $12 per 1M tokens at commit volumes (500M+ tokens/mo)

Cost & $/feature mapping (unit examples)
- In-chat summary (avg 1.2k tokens): ~1.2 * $/1M * 0.001 = $0.03 at $25/1M; $0.018 at $15/1M; $0.0096 at $8/1M
- Decision-assist (avg 3k tokens): ~$0.075 at $25/1M; $0.045 at $15/1M; $0.024 at $8/1M
- Embedding index (per doc ingest, 3k tokens equivalent): same as decision-assist above for generation cost - note embeddings have different unit pricing; we’ll surface embedding-specific numbers if that’s central.

Monthly cost examples (conservative tokens = 900M/mo)
- At $25/1M: 900 * $25 = $22.5k/mo
- At $15/1M: 900 * $15 = $13.5k/mo
- At $10/1M (mid-dedicated band): 900 * $10 = $9k/mo

Unit economics implications
- If your target budget is $30k- $80k/mo, that comfortably covers steady-state inference costs even at $25/1M; the remaining budget needs to cover hosting, data infrastructure, and SRE (client side) plus go-to-market.
- CAC payback (simple example): assume revenue per new MAU = $2/mo (example), CAC = $50, gross margin target 60% after inference & infra. Payback = CAC / (Gross contribution per month). We'll build a few variations in the one-page.

Recommendations / asks
1) If your business is cost-sensitive, commit modeling around a 6-12 month volume forecast so we can show Dedicated commit pricing that materially reduces $/1M.
2) Confirm whether embeddings will be high-volume (we'll price separately - embedding units often lower $/1k dims but different SKU).
3) If latency SLOs for decision-assist are strict (<200ms), we should scope a Dedicated footprint or reserved capacity burst policy.

Next actions
- We’ll produce a 1-page unit-econ PDF and a 2-scenario quote (hosted vs reserved) by EOD Thursday.
- Aditya can run a short eval (sample payloads) if you want latency numbers for the decision-assist flow.

Attaching: (will attach the one-page worked calcs as a PDF in next message).

Best —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
